cards.text: Moses, Israel’s leader, leads the people away from the Red Sea, where the LORD brought them through on dry ground (Exodus 14:29). They head into the Desert of Shur, and for three days they walk without finding water. That’s circling a parking garage, friend: level after level after level, and NOTHING.
At last they reach Marah, and there’s WATER, but it’s bitter, so they can’t drink it. You know when you finally find a free outlet at the airport and it’s DEAD?

cards.question: At Marah, the water is too bitter to drink. What do the people do?

cards.text: “What are we to drink?” they ask. Friend, people fall apart when the Wi-Fi drops for three MINUTES, and these folks have gone three DAYS without water.

cards.question: The people at Marah are grumbling against Moses. What does Moses do?

answers.text: He cries out to the LORD
He sends men to dig a well
He leads them back toward the sea

cards.text: And the LORD shows Moses a log. Moses casts it into the bitter water, and I’d be standing there going, friend, you’re about to make it WORSE.

cards.question: Moses has thrown the log into the bitter water at Marah. What happens to the water?

cards.text: There at Marah, the LORD makes a statute and an ordinance for them, and He tests them. Then He speaks, and His words start with “If.”

cards.question: If they listen carefully and keep His statutes, the LORD says He won’t bring on them any of the ___ He brought on the Egyptians.
At Marah, the LORD calls Himself the LORD who heals them.

cards.text: Then they move on to a place called Elim. Friend, after that last stop, I’d send somebody ahead to TASTE the water first.

cards.question: What do the Israelites find at Elim, where they camp by the waters?

answers.text: Twelve springs and seventy palm trees
Twelve stones from the Jordan River
A well dug by the princes

cards.text: On the fifteenth day of the second month after leaving Egypt, the whole congregation of Israel sets out from Elim. They come to the Desert of Sin, between Elim and Sinai.

There the whole congregation grumbles against Moses and Aaron, Moses’ brother (Exodus 4:14): “If only we had died by the LORD’s hand in the land of Egypt!” Look, my first week in the junk drawer I missed that kitchen counter so bad, I forgot it was the place I got REPLACED.

cards.question: The people say they wish they’d died in Egypt. What do they say they had back there?

answers.text: Pots of meat and plenty of bread

cards.text: They say Moses and Aaron brought them out here to starve. Then the LORD tells Moses, “Behold, I will rain down bread from heaven for you.”

cards.question: The LORD says the people are to go out and gather a whole week’s worth of the bread at a time.
The LORD says each day the people gather just enough bread for that day. Why does He set it up that way?

answers.text: To test whether they will follow His instructions
To keep the camp from getting too crowded
To teach them how to trade with each other

cards.question: The LORD says that on the sixth day, the people will bring in twice as much as on the other days.

cards.text: Moses and Aaron tell everyone that this evening they’ll know it was the LORD who brought them out of Egypt, and in the morning they’ll see the LORD’s glory. Then they ask, “For who are we, that you should grumble against us?”

cards.question: Moses says the people’s grumblings are not against him and Aaron but against the ___.

cards.text: And Moses adds that the LORD will give them meat to eat this evening and bread to fill them in the morning. Then he tells Aaron to call the whole congregation to come before the LORD, because He has heard their grumbling.

cards.question: As Aaron speaks, the congregation looks toward the desert and the glory of the LORD appears. What does it appear in?

cards.text: The LORD tells Moses He has heard the grumbling. At twilight they’ll eat meat, in the morning they’ll be filled with bread, and then they’ll know He is the LORD their God.

cards.question: That evening in the Desert of Sin, ___ come and cover the camp.

cards.text: In the morning there’s a layer of dew around the camp. When it dries up, there are thin flakes on the desert floor, as fine as frost on the ground.

cards.question: The Israelites find thin flakes on the desert floor. What do they ask one another?

cards.text: Picture the whole camp standing around it like a package nobody remembers ordering. Then Moses tells them, “It is the bread that the LORD has given you to eat.”
The LORD’s command is for each one to gather as much as he needs, an omer for each person in the tent. So they go out, and some gather more, and some gather less.

cards.question: When the Israelites measure the bread by the omer, the ones who gathered less don’t come up short.

cards.text: Then Moses gives them a rule about the bread: “No one may keep any of it until morning.” No leftovers, friend. Not even a crumb.

cards.question: Everyone listens to Moses and leaves none of the bread until morning.
Some people keep part of the bread until morning anyway. What happens to it?

answers.text: It gets maggots and starts to smell
It turns as hard as a rock
It blows away in the wind

cards.text: Maggots AND a smell, so Moses is angry with them. I lived in a junk drawer for years, friend, and even I would’ve filed a complaint.
Every morning they gather what’s needed, and when the sun grows hot, it melts away. Then on the sixth day they gather twice as much, two omers per person, and the leaders come and report it to Moses.

cards.question: The leaders tell Moses about the double portion on the sixth day. What does Moses say tomorrow is?

answers.text: A day to gather even more

cards.text: Moses passes along what the LORD said: “So bake what you want to bake, and boil what you want to boil.” Then they set the rest aside until morning, and after those maggots, friend, I’d be lifting that cover REAL slow.

cards.question: This time, the bread they set aside until morning doesn’t smell or get maggots.
Moses tells them to eat it today, because today is a Sabbath to the LORD. He says they may gather for six days. What does he say about the seventh day?

answers.text: Only half of it will fall

cards.question: When some people go out to gather on the seventh day, they find a little bread.

cards.text: They find NOTHING, like pulling on the bank door on a holiday and reading the sign through the glass. Then the LORD says to Moses, “How long will you refuse to keep My commandments and instructions?”

cards.question: The LORD says He has given them the Sabbath, and on the seventh day everyone must ___ where he is.

cards.text: So the people rest on the seventh day. The house of Israel calls the bread manna, and it’s white like coriander seed.
It tastes like wafers made with honey. Friend, I’ve stamped cookies my whole life, and I could NEVER top that.

cards.question: Moses says the LORD has commanded them to keep an omer of manna. What is it for?

answers.text: So future generations can see it
So they have food if it runs out
So Aaron can offer it on the altar

cards.text: So Aaron fills a jar with an omer of manna and places it in front of the Testimony, to be preserved just as the LORD commanded Moses.

cards.question: The Israelites eat manna until they reach the border of Canaan, for forty ___.

cards.text: And in case you were wondering, an omer is a tenth of an ephah. I’m putting that on a sticky note on my oven, friend, because I am NOT doing that math in my head.
